one_liner: Pylon (usepylon.com) has a REST API with admin-created bearer tokens, plus an official OAuth MCP server, but API access appears to need a paid seat-based plan with an annual contract.
auth_notes: The REST API uses bearer API tokens created by an Admin under Settings > Integrations & dev > API. Tokens don't expire and have no scopes. OAuth 2.0 exists only for the vendor's MCP server, not for the REST API, and there is no documented self-serve app registration.
access_notes: Pricing lists the API as included in the Professional plan ($89 per seat/month, annual contract). No free tier or trial is evidenced. Only Admins can create tokens.
blocker_notes: The API is documented, but getting a working token requires a paid Pylon workspace on an annual contract. The evidence shows no free tier or trial. A sales-assisted route may exist, which is unverified.

evidence.quote: The Pylon API uses [Bearer](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6750#section-2.1) authentication. This means you’ll need to pass your API token in the header of your request
Tokens don't expire, and their access is controlled only by the role. There are no separate scopes.
Professional** | **$89 per seat/month**, annual contract | Core support, viewer seats, analytics, automations, Skills, broadcasts, MCP, API, integrations
Only Admins can create and manage API tokens.
Developer platform:** REST API, scoped API tokens, webhooks, iFrame embeds, custom apps, Pylon MCP server.
The Pylon MCP Server exposes Pylon data to AI tools that support the Model Context Protocol (e.g. Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor).
The Pylon MCP server only supports OAuth authentication. API key authentication is not currently available
